routes.label: Multiply the remaining fraction five times

question:
An equilateral triangle is originally painted black. Each time the triangle is changed, the middle fourth of each black triangle turns white. After five changes, what fractional part of the original area of the black triangle remains black?

[Figure 1](figures/1991_AMC_8_Q25_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Track the total black area instead of counting the small triangles. Each black triangle loses \(\frac14\) of its area, so it keeps \(1-\frac14=\frac34\). Since this happens to every black triangle, the total black area also becomes \(\frac34\) of what it was before the change.

Starting with the entire original area, five changes leave the fraction
\[
\frac34\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac34
=\left(\frac34\right)^5
=\frac{243}{1024}.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{\frac{243}{1024}}\) remains black, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
